hawkish.text: According to the Statistics Poland flash estimate, in September 2026 CPI inflation increased to 4.0% y/y (from 3.4% y/y in August).

NBP will continue to take all necessary actions in order to ensure macroeconomic and financial stability, including above all to ensure inflation at the level consistent with the NBP inflation target in the medium term.

The shape of fiscal policy, regulatory decisions regarding energy prices, changes in activity growth of the Polish economy and further developments in wage growth also remain risk factors for inflation outlook.
At the same time, due to higher energy commodity prices, global inflation is higher than at the beginning of 2026.
This was mainly due to the rise in the annual growth in prices of fuels for personal transport equipment.

dovish.text: At the same time, it can be estimated that in September inflation net of food and energy prices declined somewhat.
At the same time, a fall in employment in this sector, is continuing.
Wage growth in the enterprise sector in August – after a rise in July – decreased.
In 2026 Q2, annual GDP growth rate in the euro area accelerated, and in the United States it slowed down, but was running close to its long-term average.

rows.text: The Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged:

rows.text: At the same time, due to higher energy commodity prices, global inflation is higher than at the beginning of 2026.
The outlook for global activity and inflation is subject to uncertainty, stemming, in particular, from the conflict in the Middle East.
In Poland, in August 2026 retail sales, industrial output as well as construction and assembly production increased in annual terms.
rows.prev_text: In July 2026, retail sales and industrial output increased in annual terms, while construction and assembly production declined.

rows.text: Wage growth in the enterprise sector in August – after a rise in July – decreased.
At the same time, a fall in employment in this sector, is continuing.

rows.text: Against this background the Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged.
Further decisions of the Council will depend on incoming information regarding prospects for inflation and economic activity in Poland.
Particularly important is macroeconomic situation abroad, including developments in global commodity prices and inflation, amid changing geopolitical context.

The shape of fiscal policy, regulatory decisions regarding energy prices, changes in activity growth of the Polish economy and further developments in wage growth also remain risk factors for inflation outlook.
